test_title: PYST 17: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which Article of the Constitution of India prevents any child below the age of 14 years from being employed in the factory, mine or hazardous occupation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 24** of the Constitution of India prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any hazardous occupations.
 
• This provision is part of the fundamental rights under the **Right against Exploitation** outlined in the Constitution.
 
• The article aims to protect children from exploitation and hazardous working conditions that can harm their physical and mental health.
 
• It aligns with the government's commitment to ensuring the welfare and development of children by preventing child labor in unsafe environments.
 
• India has ratified international conventions such as the **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child** and the **ILO Convention No. 182** to combat child labor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Labor Prohibition and Regulation Act, 1986:**

 
 
• This act regulates the working conditions for children and prohibits their employment in hazardous occupations.
 
• It defines hazardous occupations and processes where child labor is strictly prohibited.
 
 
 
• **The Right to Education Act, 2009:**
 
 
• This act ensures free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years, thereby indirectly combating child labor.
 
• Education is seen as a key tool to prevent children from being exploited in the workforce.
 
 
 
• **National Child Labor Project (NCLP):**
 
 
• Under this initiative, children withdrawn from hazardous work are enrolled in special schools to provide education, nutrition, and vocational training.
 
• The program aims to rehabilitate child laborers and integrate them into the mainstream education system.
 
 
 
• **International Initiatives:**
 
 
• India is a signatory to the **ILO Minimum Age Convention (No. 138)**, which sets the minimum age for employment.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** also emphasize the elimination of child labor under Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).
